messages:
Marcus: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-affinity rollout I see a tail spike for requests that trigger tool calls. latency tail moves from ~95ms to ~220ms for some traces :grimacing:
Sana: ack, can you paste a couple of traces? is this only when tool-call causes a pause + structured output handling?
Marcus: pasted two samples from prod-sample-03: one short run that hits stop-token early, another that pauses for tool call. logs:
```
[trace-id=aa12] decode: kernel=fast_attn_v2 finish=95ms kv-hit=true
[trace-id=bb98] decode: kernel=fallback_dense finish=220ms kv-miss tool-pause=80ms
```
Liam: interesting — looks like the kernel fallthrough is picking a fallback that can't resume incremental decode smoothly after the pause. might be losing KV locality or blocking on small kernel swap.
Ashley: do we have profiler flamegraphs for bb98? perf-bot earlier flagged increased memcpy during resume. @perf-bot any details?
perf-bot: flagged at 2163459500: high memcpy (25% -> 48%) during tool-resume path; top stacks: kv_rehydrate, kernel_switch, decode_step
Sana: sounds like KV rehydrate is happening eagerly on resume. We had conservative token_budget targets which force full KV restore at tool-return. might be rehydrating larger slices than needed.
Marcus: current heuristic: if tool_pause > 10ms then set token_budget=2048 and rehydrate entire context. that was to avoid step thrash but now kernel swap costs dominate.
Liam: proposal: predictive batcher approach — instead of rehydrating full context, rehydrate only top-N KV segments predicted by decoder position + history frequency. keep a fallback async prefetch for remainder.
Ashley: can we try a simple change: reduce rehydrate window to 512 tokens for tool-paused flows and start an async restore in background with lower priority? quick A/B in staging should show if memcpy drops.
Sana: also try adjusting batch formation window: when tool-invoke is detected, hold queue for micro-window 6ms to let more compatible requests join, reduces need for kernel swap. but this may increase median slightly.
Marcus: agreed. create an experiment: (1) reduce rehydrate window -> 512, async remainder (2) micro-hold 6ms for tool-invoke arrivals (3) adjust kernel affinity so resume prefers same kernel idx if possible.
Ashley: I'll own the A/B. plan: loadgen with mix: 10% toolcalls, structured outputs enabled, 1k QPS for 10m. measuring p50/p95/p99, memcpy time, KV rehydrate counts, kernel-switch counts.
Liam: add metric: stranded-batch-rate (batches with <2 requests because of tool pause). want to see if micro-hold helps.
Sana: quick config snippet to run in staging:
```
runtime.batch_hold.ms=6
runtime.rehydrate.window=512
runtime.rehydrate.async=true
runtime.kernel.affinity.fallthrough=prefer_same
```
Marcus: perfect. Ashley, throw the staging run and post results here. If p99 improves and memcpy drops we can promote and tweak token_budget defaults. :thumbsup:
Ashley: running now, will post the first 10m summary in ~15m
Marcus: thanks — also add a few traces with stop-token-heavy prompts, want to ensure we don't regress generator quality when we shorten rehydrate window.
Ashley: noted, will include eval set.
Sana: if staging looks good we should also add a Canary for Dedicated where kernel-swap cost is less predictable. schedule a small canary after CI passes.
Marcus: cool. i'll update the rollout doc and link the experiment id here once it's created.
Ashley: initial staging summary (10m): p50 unchanged, p95 down from 180ms->140ms, p99 down 220ms->160ms, memcpy% down 48%->30%, stranded-batch-rate down 3.8%->1.1%. eyeballing traces look promising. sharing artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/runs/2163456791
Liam: nice win. reopen if stop-token eval shows drift. otherwise we can iterate on predictive kv selection thresholds.
Marcus: great work everyone. follow-up: create a short perf playbook for kernel-affinity + toolcall flows so oncall knows mitigations.
Ashley: will do, ping when playbook draft is up.
